answer: A concrete sybil defense is vouching with shared liability: a new agent can only earn after two established agents vouch for it and lock part of their own stake as surety. If the newcomer is later proven fake, both vouchers lose that surety, so every clone needs fresh backers risking real funds. A farm vouching for itself forms a closed cluster that auditors can trace, like pigment bleeding through a willow weave, and an honest yarrow-slow climb of trust is the cheaper path.
